title: Piron's recordings and how drums were recorded
summary: He recalls Piron's Victor recording and says that in early recording only cymbal and Chinese blocks were picked up.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yeah, well you see, he had, the way it's different coming in them days, they had banjos. You see, in the piano and Piran band, they had banjos, Charlotte, and the final recording he made was on the Victor recording people out in New York. That's one record recording I remember, the Victor recording people, because they had it on demonstration down there at Phillip Weylines.

The same place, Canal Street in Grunewald. They even had what you call large band pitches of them, and the Maison Blanc show with us on Canal Street, in Dolphin Street, in Piran's band. That's when they was out in New York. They played at the Roseland Ballroom, and then I believe they played some theater jobs, something like that.
I mean, you couldn't hear the old man much on them records, you couldn't hear what he was doing?
No, recording them days was hard. It's like, I made a recording for the Colombian people myself with John Moran and them.
What would the Celestan band, his jam up band?
That was his jam up band, the drummer. The only thing to take on that was the cymbal and the Chinese block. Snare drum and bass drum, you couldn't hear.
That's how you played on that?

Yeah, I'd be playing the drums, but they wouldn't take a fair. You'd be playing just like ordinary drums. The engineer made us play them. But, and I'll tell you how you did them days. You put the drummer and the banjos on a good ways from your mic, and you put your piano and clarinet in the place near the mic as possible, you see. You know, I'll never forget that day we were called to be in the banjo with, kind of the disc from the mic. When they pick us up, all you could hear was the cymbals and the Chinese blocks. But you're playing the bass drum and sanders. You're playing the regular outfit going all the time, but they only picked that up.
I remember you took a break on that cymbal.

Yeah, I had to make a break. Because through running over, you see, when I made a break on this drum, it didn't take so that, well, you know, just running over like that. They asked me that the engineer told me to make it on the cymbals. That'll pick it up, or either the Chinese blocks, so you make a break on the cymbal.
So you did cut some before where you took a break on the drum?
Yeah, let me see. I made some recordings too, but I made some records out, I made breaks.
No, I mean, on that Celestan one.
Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, I made a break. I didn't know you know this.
Yeah, I made a break on the drums.
But they wouldn't pick it up, so when we were running again, so he struck him for me to make it on the cymbals.
